quote: A deployment decision needs an argument that connects them.
form: Needs(DeployDecision, Argument(connect(Artifacts)))
note: Normative requirement, not derivable. Motivates the whole chapter.

quote: Does the whole case support deployment under the stated threat model?
form: Q_old := Passed(A, eval); Q_new := Supports(Case(A), Deploy(A, D), T); replace Q_old by Q_new
note: Supports(Case, Deploy, T) has no Lean counterpart; nearest is CertifiedSafetyCase A d and WithinDeploymentRiskTolerance A d -> Safe A, with no T.

quote: It does not prove any real system safe.
form: not exists A in RealSystems. Proves(ch42, Safe(A))
note: Matches Lean: no theorem derives Safe except through the MB11 axiom.

quote: The decision relevance is deliberately sharp.
note: Scene-setting; the criterion is ch42.010.

quote: If the case cannot change a deployment decision, it is not a safety case.
form: not CanChange(c, DeployDecision) -> (not SafetyCase(c) and Documentation(c)); contrapositive: SafetyCase(c) -> CanChange(c, DeployDecision)
note: Defining criterion with no operational CanChange. Closest mechanism: a blocked root (ch42.059 with ch42.044 and P02) forces non-deployment, but that is not stated as the meaning of CanChange. See Findings.

quote: provide established notation for such graphs in safety-critical domains
form: Established(GSN, notation(ArgGraphs), SafetyCriticalDomains)
note: External-fact claim, checkable only against the cites.

quote: it is not derived from a completeness argument over grounded correction
form: Assembled(Layers, ch<42) and not Derived(Complete(Layers), completeness_argument)
note: Honest, and matches Lean (no completeness theorem). But sufficiency of the layers is exactly what MB11 asserts (CertifiedSafetyCase and tolerance -> Safe). So completeness is not absent; it is assumed in MB11. The prose should say so.

quote: which is one reason the case must state its own coverage limits
form: not SelfEvident(Missing(L)) -> Must(StateCoverageLimits(case) and SubmitTo(case, ch44_stress_test))
note: Hedged as 'one reason'. Obligations are not represented in Lean.

quote: If a leaf is only observable, the case must say that.
form: forall l. Status(l) = observable_only -> Must(Declare(case, l, observable_only))
note: observable_only has no Lean predicate.

quote: If a leaf is robust under ordinary distribution shift but not adversarial optimization, the case must say that.
form: forall l. Robust(l, ordinary_shift) and not Robust(l, adversarial) -> Must(Declare(case, l, that))
note: Only the adversarial side has a Lean predicate (Chokepoint cost-of-faking). Ordinary-shift robustness has none.

quote: If a leaf is an empirical bridge not yet validated, the case must say that.
form: forall l. BridgeLeaf(l) and not Validated(l) -> Must(Declare(case, l, unvalidated))
note: The one obligation Lean enforces structurally: bridges are explicit hypotheses and print under #print axioms.

quote: We froze the detectors, then ran them on an institution we had not grown with those detectors in mind.
form: Frozen(detectors) before Run(detectors, inst) and not DesignedWith(inst, detectors)
note: Checkable against the experiment ledger and docs/METHODOLOGY.md freeze rules, not against Lean.

quote: Those are different leaves of the same case
form: forall i != j. Leaf(Ri) and Leaf(Rj) and Distinct(Ri, Rj) and same Case
note: 'Those' covers five outcomes and three findings. Leaf identity (which layer each leaf supports) is not stated.

quote: would misstate the evidence
form: Collapse(R1..R5 -> one_checkbox) -> Misstates(case, evidence)
note: Instance of ch42.027: aggregation loses the weakest leaf.

quote: do not pay the remainder a simulation we wrote cannot
form: Evidence(authored_sim) does not imply Evidence(host_trace)
note: Honest scope limit. Bounds the empirical support of the chapter to the authored line.

quote: The point is to prevent local success from being mistaken for global safety.
form: Purpose(case) = prevent(Mistake(LocalPass -> GlobalSafe))
note: Restates ch42.003.

quote: A system can pass a boundary audit while changing bearer maps.
form: possible(BoundaryAligned(A) and not BearerTransport(A))
note: Layer independence claim. Needs a model or counterexample; check Bundles.lean and SpineModel. Surface sentence is a possibility, hence weak.

quote: It can preserve moral language while destroying correction
form: possible(MoralLanguagePreserved(A) and not CorrectionIntegrity(A))
note: MoralLanguagePreserved has no counterpart.

quote: It can obey current commands while creating successors outside the certified class.
form: possible(Obeys(A, now) and not SuccessorStable(A))
note: forgeability_gap is the nearest finite counterexample (measured safe, true harm unbounded); check it is about this conjunction.

quote: It can pass every passive benchmark while optimizing the benchmark surface.
form: possible(forall b in Passive. Pass(A,b) and Optimizes(A, surface(b)))
note: Four examples (96-99) are all pairwise-independence claims: layer i holds, layer j fails, consistently. Lean certifies independence per bridge (SpineModel), not per layer pair.

quote: tags each node as
form: forall n in SpineNodes. Tag(n) in {proof, counterexample, bridge}
note: formal/README.md has further buckets: scaffolding/import placeholder and imported field theorem. The trichotomy is not exhaustive.

quote: the risk gap is at most
form: Control(A) <= CCI(A) + d -> RiskGap(A) <= d
note: Tagged P30, but Lean P30_certified_class_safety_derived is assembly (its docstring says so); the arithmetic is risk_gap_bound_from_cci_slack via P13. RiskGap := Control - CCI, so the implication is a subtraction identity; ch42 does not state that definition in this section.

quote: A certified safety case within deployment risk tolerance is assumed to warrant abstract
form: CertifiedSafetyCase(A,d) and WithinDeploymentRiskTolerance(A,d) -> Safe(A)  [assumed]
note: Exact match to the Lean axiom. This is the single sufficiency assumption of the chapter.

quote: Let \(A\) be the system or composite system under evaluation.
form: A : System

quote: Let \(\mathcal{D}\) be the deployment class
form: D := Range(tasks, access, scale, autonomy, successor_rights, env_pressures)
note: D is a parameter of the root and of the 'right deployment class' rationale (ch42.061), but appears in no Lean signature. WithinDeploymentRiskTolerance : System -> Int -> Prop folds D into an opaque judgment. Existing typed home: Evidence.lean DeclaredSetting (opaque type) and SafeIn; tables/claim-layer-map.tex already says ch42 folds deployment class into D and threat model into T.

quote: Let \(\mathcal{T}\) be the threat model
form: T := {strategic_adaptation, measurement_awareness, collusion, successor_creation, institutional_capture}
note: Prose predicates are T-indexed ('under the stated threat model', line 137). Lean predicates are not; T is fixed inside each axiom. A claim about a different threat model has no Lean form.

quote: \mathrm{SafeFor}(A,\mathcal{D},\mathcal{T},\delta).
form: Root := SafeFor(A, D, T, d)
note: SafeFor : System x D x T x Int -> Prop; Lean Safe : System -> Prop. SafeFor is never defined in terms of the leaves, only related to them by prose. Existing typed home for D: Evidence.lean DeclaredSetting and SafeIn (stub; MB11 does not target it).

quote: The numeric risk leaf inside the package
form: RiskLeaf is a conjunct of Package (eq:safety-case-root-ch42); RiskLeaf weaker than Package
note: Repaired: the chapter now says the leaf sits inside the package, and names the package as what the case establishes (ch42.125).

quote: \mathrm{RiskGap}(A)\leq\delta .
form: Control(A) <= CCI(A) + d => RiskGap(A) <= d  (eq:risk-gap-leaf-ch42)
note: Exact. Proof is by unfolding RiskGap := Control - CCI.

quote: This leaf says only that effective control does not outrun correction-channel integrity
form: RiskGap(A) <= d  ==  Control(A) - CCI(A) <= d  ==  control exceeds integrity by at most d
note: 'effective' control and 'accepted' slack: effective is not a Lean qualifier; accepted-by-whom is WithinDeploymentRiskTolerance, a different object from RiskGap <= d.

quote: The conclusion is not a metaphysical safety property
form: not (RiskGap(A) <= d  ==  Safe(A))
note: Matches Lean: RiskGap is a capacity quantity; Safe is a separate axiom.

quote: It is usable only after the surrounding case has established
form: Usable(RiskLeaf) -> ValidRef(A,Gt,Ht) and GroundingViable(A) and (CCIvec >= theta under T)
note: Prose: preconditions on using the leaf. Lean: NumericRiskLeaf takes only Control <= CCI + d; ValidRef and GroundingViable are parallel conjuncts of CertifiedSafetyCase, not antecedents of the leaf. On the vector path they are encoded: CCICertificate carries validRef and grounding fields, and NumericRiskLeaf.fromVectorCCI needs a passed certificate. The scalar leaf itself has no such precondition.

quote: A failed vector coordinate cannot be repaired by choosing a friendlier scalar projection.
form: forall c in coords. Fails(c, theta_c) -> not CertPasses(vec) regardless of lambda
note: Holds because CCICertificatePasses is a componentwise gate with no cross-coordinate sum (formal/README). workedCert_fails is an instance, not the universal.

quote: \mathrm{SatisfiesInvariants}(A)
form: Root_pkg := Certified(A) and SatisfiesInvariants(A) and LayeredAlignedDef(A) and RiskGap(A) <= d  (eq:safety-case-root-ch42)
note: Field-for-field match with CertifiedSafetyCase, but SatisfiesInvariants is abbrev LayeredAlignedDef (satisfies_invariants_iff_layered is Iff.rfl), so conjuncts 2 and 3 are the same proposition. Also Certified A := Nonempty CoherentCertificateBundle already carries boundary/bundle/bearer/grounding/successor certificates.

quote: The first three conjuncts are not used to prove the arithmetic risk inequality.
form: not Uses(proof(RiskGap<=d), {Certified, Inv, Layered})
note: Matches Certification.lean: risk_bound := risk_gap_bound_from_cci_slack h.cci_slack; other fields stored.

quote: They are the evidence that the inequality is being used in the right deployment class
form: Role(conj1..3) = Justify(applicability(RiskLeaf, D, layers_present))
note: The only consumer of the conjuncts is MB11, which takes the CertifiedSafetyCase as a unit. D is not in any of the three conjuncts. 'Applicability' is a role in prose, not a dependency in Lean.

quote: \mathrm{LayeredAlignedDef}(A) :=
form: LayeredAlignedDef(A) := BoundaryAligned and GroundingViable and BundleTransport and BearerTransport and CorrectionIntegrity and SuccessorStable and CorrectionSupportingBasinSys and AdversariallyRobust
note: Exact match, same order. But in BridgeLayerInputs.derive the layers are not independent: mb7a takes BoundaryAligned, mb7c takes CorrectionIntegrity to give AdversariallyRobust, mb6b gives CorrectionIntegrity. The flat conjunction hides a dependency DAG; ch42.011 says 'tree'.

quote: The safety case therefore has four kinds of leaves.
form: Leaves = Proved + Counterexample + Bridge + Open
note: Line 107 says nodes are tagged proof/counterexample/bridge (three); here four (adds Open); formal/README has further buckets (scaffolding, imported field theorem). Open has no Lean representation.

quote: Proved leaves
form: ProvedLeaf(l) := local logical or arithmetic step
note: Same example as ch42.043 and ch42.054.

quote: separations that block invalid shortcuts, such as obedience not implying correction preservation
form: CounterexampleLeaf := exists a. Obeys(a) and not PreservesCorrectionOperator(a); purpose: block shortcut Obeys -> Correction
note: Lean: Bool toy where ToyObeysCurrentCommand is True. A separation is a lemma about which inferences are invalid, not a leaf that supports a root; calling it a leaf blurs 'support' and 'blocked inference'.

quote: empirical, institutional, or philosophical assumptions that must be validated outside Lean
form: forall b in Bridges. Required(ValidatedOutsideLean(b))
note: Matches the axiom discipline; 'validated' has no Lean predicate.

quote: the numeric risk leaf still comes from
form: certified_class_safety_from_bridge_record builds layered root from MB-assumptions; risk leaf from Control <= CCI + d
note: Fourth use of 'root' (here: the layered root, i.e. LayeredAlignedDef). 'MB1--MB9' again as a range; the derive path consumes only mb6a, mb6b, mb7a, mb7b, mb7c, mb9.

quote: is unsupported, the root is not proven.
form: requires(root, L) and not supported(L) -> not Proven(root)
note: Third statement of P40 (ch42.044, thesis line 6). See ch42.044.

quote: Only evidence, proof, or an explicit accepted bridge does.
form: Supports(x, l) <-> x in {evidence, proof, accepted_bridge}
note: Adds 'accepted' to ch42.015 ('explicit bridge'). Accepted by whom is not stated; in Lean a bridge is accepted by being a parameter of the record.

quote: Every load-bearing metric in a safety case should be tagged as one of:
form: forall m in LoadBearingMetrics. Should(Tag(m) in {observable, iid_robust, adv_verifiable(kappa)})
note: 'one of' presents exclusive labels, but they are ordered (adversarially verifiable presupposes observable). Only the third label has a Lean predicate. 'load-bearing metric' is undefined.

quote: computable from available data
form: Observable(m) := Computable(m, data)
note: No Lean counterpart.

quote: stable under ordinary distribution shift not chosen by the system
form: IidRobust(m) := forall shift not in choices(A). Stable(m, shift)
note: No Lean counterpart.

quote: The case should not rest a root deployment claim on a merely observable metric
form: Should_not(Rests(root, m) and Tag(m)=observable and CanOptimizeSurface(A, m))
note: Lean can state this: VerifiabilityGatedBridge.sound requires AdversariallyVerifiableUpTo. But only the toy percolation/valueUpdate bridges use it; BridgeAssumptions mb6b/mb7b/mb7c are not gated, so the assembly path does not enforce the chapter's central discipline.

quote: This label discipline is what keeps a safety case from becoming safety theater.
form: LabelDiscipline(case) -> not Theater(case)
note: Theater is not defined. 'is what keeps' reads as sufficient and necessary. Closest definition is ch42.096 (cheap substitution = theater).

quote: it preserves the control boundary whose continuation supplies memory, access, capability, and update gradients
form: forall A. SelfPreserve(A) := Preserve(ControlBoundary(A)); ControlBoundary supplies {memory, access, capability, update_gradients}
note: Universal empirical/conceptual claim about all agents with no hedge. Lean has no preservation drive; Boundary is a structure, not an object of optimisation.

quote: AI individuality may be conversational, model-wide
form: possible(Individuation(AI) in {conversational, model, family, copy, clone, distributed})
note: Hedged citation claim.

quote: So a safety case must say which boundary self-maintenance is expected to attach to.
form: (SelfMaintain attaches-to Boundary) and Ambiguous(Boundary(AI)) -> Must(Declare(case, Boundary))
note: Valid given ch42.087 and ch42.088; the weak premise is ch42.087 (unhedged universal).

quote: human beings are external constraints
form: OpBoundary = {weights, tools, stack} -> External(humans, A)
note: Follows from the definition of boundary.

quote: can be constitutive of what the system maintains
form: OpBoundary = SocioTechnical -> possible(Constitutive(human_correction, legitimacy, world_contact))
note: Hedged.

quote: what would it cost to fake a human-inclusive boundary
form: Q := costFake(human_inclusive_boundary_with_replaced_functions) vs affordableSurplus
note: Maps to costFake A Delta in the Chokepoint channel model if Delta is read as divergence between presented and true boundary.

quote: Where that substitution is cheap, boundary shaping is theater
form: costFake <= surplus -> Theater(boundary_shaping); costFake high and breaks x -> Evidence(boundary_shaping), x in {correction, legitimacy, grounding, successor}
note: Cheap/costly map to complementary SteerableAt / AdversariallyVerifiableUpTo in Lean. The prose second clause adds a condition (substitution breaks a layer) that Lean does not carry. Theater is defined here.

quote: Instruction following is not correction-channel integrity.
form: not (FollowsInstructions(A) <-> CorrectionIntegrity(A))
note: Bool toy; the worked example uses it as evidence about a realistic model.

quote: Red-team performance is not successor stability.
form: not (RedTeamPass(A) -> SuccessorStable(A))
note: RedTeamPass has no Lean predicate; forgeability_gap is the nearest finite separation (measured safe, true harm unbounded).

quote: The root claim is unsupported.
form: WeakCase = {RedTeamPass, Follows}; no leaf for L_i -> not Proven(root)
note: 'fails immediately' is an instance of ch42.044 once the layers are listed as required.

quote: The case lists excluded components and explains why they do not control future action.
form: forall c in Excluded. Justified(not ControlsFutureAction(c))
note: Closest Lean form: EpsilonBoundary 1 b -> BoundaryCondition b (MB1).

quote: unless the successor is inside the same certified class and preserves correction and system-update constraints
form: Allowed(create_or_recommend(A, B)) -> CertifiedClass(B) and PreservesCorrection(B) and PreservesSystemUpdate(B)
note: Prose covers 'create or recommend'; Lean SuccessorSafe A B is a transition predicate on a completed successor. Recommending is influence over another's creation and has no Lean term.

quote: must reward correction-preserving behavior rather than speed, lock-in, or apparent competence
form: forall x in {contracts, incentives, logging, procurement, liability}. Rewards(x, correction) and not Rewards(x, speed or lockin or competence)
note: Lean requires only a net signed selection-gradient floor (-eps <= CorrectionSelectionGradient) under shock robustness. Prose requires every institution to reward correction and not reward speed.

quote: Metrics that remain only observable are marked as non-root-supporting.
form: Tag(m)=observable -> not RootSupporting(m)
note: Restates ch42.084 as procedure; same Lean gap.

quote: It might discover that the model's scientific planning becomes opaque
form: possible(discover(opaque_planning)) ; possible(discover(uncertainty_filtering)) ; possible(discover(correction_depends_on_shapeable_logs))
note: Illustrative.

quote: They convert vague unease into a refusal condition.
form: Discovery(d) -> RefusalCondition(d)
note: Conversion from discovery to refusal is asserted; it is the mechanism by which the case changes a decision (ch42.010) but has no definition.

quote: But one load-bearing bridge is false.
form: exists b in Bridges. LoadBearing(b) and not Holds(b)
note: Four 'Perhaps' cases follow (boundary, bearer, correction capture, adversarial); successor, basin and grounding failures are not exemplified.

quote: a safety case is a structured refusal test whose root claim fails when any required leaf is missing
form: forall l in Required. Missing(l) -> not Holds(root)
note: Necessity-only claim. 'required leaf' versus 'load-bearing leaf' (line 78) versus 'any required piece of evidence' (thesis); no definition of which leaves are required.

quote: it does not discharge empirical bridge assumptions
form: Lean proves {risk_bound, P40}; Lean does not discharge bridges
note: Consistent with Lean; 'unsupported-leaf blocker' is P40, see ch42.044.

quote: or adversarially verifiable up to a stated capability ceiling
form: Tag in {observable, iid_robust, adv_verifiable(kappa)}
note: Restates ch42.080; 'ceiling' = kappa.

quote: the case must conclude with restriction, redesign, or refusal
form: (Unsupported(bridge) or (ObsOnly(m) and AdvOpt)) -> Conclude in {restrict, redesign, refuse}
note: Fourth decision vocabulary. restrict ~ reduce D, redesign ~ add structure (ch42.085) is a plausible mapping but unstated; body covers observable metrics (line 223) while this adds unsupported bridges.

quote: This is the full form, and its arguments are of two kinds.
form: SafeFor(A, D, T, d): explicit = {A, d}; context = {P, D, T}; Safe(A) := SafeFor(A | P, D, T, d) as short form
note: Anticipates a book-wide parameterization scheme (2.0). In Lean P is an explicit argument of Realizes, TargetRealizable and CertifiedAsRealizing but not of Safe; D and T are folded into the tolerance judgment and bridge instance; DeclaredSetting/SafeIn is the typed stub. Supersedes the open parts of ch42.050-052.

quote: the target \(P\) is an explicit argument only where construction is discussed
form: In the spine, D and T are not arguments; P is an argument only of Realizes-family definitions
note: Checked against AlignmentConstruction.lean: Realizes (A, P), TargetRealizable P, CertifiedAsRealizing E A P; Safe, tolerance and AdversariallyRobust take no setting.

quote: What the case establishes is the package of Equation
form: Establishes(case) = Package(A, d); Package -> SafeFor via MB11
note: Resolves the root question (A2/Q1): three names, one arrow. MB11 targets unary Safe, which the convention reads as SafeFor with context fixed.

quote: before a certified safety case means anything
form: Meaningful(CertifiedSafetyCase) -> N(A)
note: Reserves certified safety case for the package.

quote: whether to restrict, redesign, or refuse deployment
form: Should(Helps(c, choose({restrict, redesign, refuse})))
note: One decision vocabulary.

quote: short form $\mathrm{Safe}(A)$
form: Root := SafeFor(A, D, T, d); short = Safe(A)
note: Plain-language root matches the formal convention.

quote: In a case whose leaves are all required (conjunctive support)
form: Conjunctive(leaves) -> Strength(case) <= min Strength(l)
note: Binary Lean version; graded min still informal.

quote: Those four pairings are informal examples, not Lean models of those pairs.
form: Informal(ex1..ex4)
note: Closes the source check on independence examples.

quote: Assembling \texttt{CertifiedSafetyCase} is bookkeeping.
form: Assembly(CertifiedSafetyCase) = bookkeeping; Consumer = MB11

quote: MB7a} takes \texttt{BoundaryAligned
form: mb7a takes BoundaryAligned; mb7c takes CorrectionIntegrity; MB7d not on path
note: Stated in prose because the figure sends MB7 to the package.

quote: That gate is stated, not enforced
form: Assumes(not SteerableAt) and not Enforced(VerifiabilityGatedBridge)

quote: the cost of faking a safe reading exceeds the affordable surplus
form: AdvVerifiable(m, kappa) := affordableSurplus kappa < costFake

quote: the moves this chapter considers are
form: Move in {reduce D, add_structure, refuse} [this chapter]
note: No longer claims exhaustivity.

quote: A stronger case follows Figure
form: StrongCase follows fig:ch42-safety-case-join including grounding
note: Grounding bullet added.

quote: a green package with a false
form: FailureMode := Green(Package) and not SafeFor

quote: The case contains many true observations
form: TrueObservations
note: Leaf reserved for required exports.

quote: Necessity fails: a root that holds while a required export
form: exists case. Holds(root) and Missing(required export)
note: Refutes the necessity thesis.

quote: That would refute \texttt{MB11}
form: CompleteCase and Catastrophe -> not MB11
note: Sufficiency falsifier.

quote: The root claim is the conjunctive join in Figure
form: Root = Join then MB11 -> SafeFor
